sections.html:
Two courthouse offices split the work. The Supervisor of Assessments and the Board of Review set and review values, and the Collector/Treasurer bills and takes payment. Both are in the Coles County Courthouse at 651 Jackson Ave in Charleston, with the Board of Review in Room 133 and the treasurer in Room 124.

Complaint forms go to the Supervisor of Assessments office, which is open from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays. The treasurer keeps the same hours and can be reached at (217) 348-0513.

  • Value, exemptions and appeals: Supervisor of Assessments and the three member Board of Review.
  • Bills, payments and the delinquent list: Coles County Collector/Treasurer.
  • Online look-up: the county's property tax inquiry portal shows assessment and tax data by parcel.

sections.h2: Coles County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Coles County is a prairie county of about 508 square miles in east central Illinois. Charleston is the seat and the home of Eastern Illinois University, and Mattoon is the other large city. The population is estimated at 46,607 for July 2025, down from 53,873 in 2010.

There are 22,693 housing units, and 60.4% of homes are owner occupied. The median owner occupied home is worth $127,400, median gross rent is $780, and monthly owner costs run $1,220 with a mortgage and $546 without one.

sections.h2: Tax dates in the Coles County cycle
sections.html:
Bills go out in the spring, with the first installment due around July 1 and the second around September 1. Late payments carry a 1.5% penalty unless the envelope is postmarked by the due date. Each year the treasurer posts exact dates on the Key Dates page, so use that page for the current cycle.

Typical Coles County tax calendar
EventTiming
Tax bills mailedMid-May
First installment dueJuly 1
Penalty on first installmentThe day after it is due
Second installment dueSeptember 1
Penalty increases on both installmentsEarly September and early October
Delinquent list published, last day to register for the saleEarly October
Tax sale, 11:30 a.m.Late October

The county splits each year's tax into two equal installments. Take a mailed payment inside the post office to be hand stamped, because a drop in a street box does not guarantee the right postmark.

sections.h2: How to pay a Coles County tax bill
sections.html:
Bring the original bill to the treasurer's office, which takes cash, checks and most credit cards. A payment drop box sits at the south entrance of the courthouse, and a second one is at Mattoon City Hall. Mail goes to the Coles County Collector, 651 Jackson Ave., Room 124, Charleston, IL 61920.

  • Banks: First Mid-Illinois Bank & Trust, Prospect Bank in Ashmore, First Farmers Bank & Trust in Oakland, Washington Savings Bank in Mattoon and several others are authorized pay points.
  • By card: phone 1-217-292-6625 or use the county tax portal at colescountyilretax.us. The card company charges a convenience fee, and an online check costs $1.00.
  • Prepayment: the treasurer accepts prepayments of any amount starting January 1, though it advises against paying more than last year's tax.

The last day for personal checks and card or e-check payments falls a couple of weeks before the sale, so pay early if you are close to the delinquent list.

You appeal the assessed value, never the tax bill, and you start with the Board of Review. The board opens its session on the first Monday in June. The 2026 filing deadline is December 14, 2026, and the complaint forms say the deadline is 30 days after the Supervisor of Assessments publishes the assessments.

An early call to the assessor can sometimes fix a clerical error without a hearing. A written complaint to the Board of Review is required before any later appeal to the state Property Tax Appeal Board, and taxes stay payable while that appeal is pending. The state board's number is 217-782-6076.

  • A recent purchase on the open market or a professional appraisal supports a claim that the value is too high.
  • A wrong lot or building measurement is another ground.
  • Comparable homes, property record cards, photographs and a transfer declaration make up the evidence package.

Once the tax bill arrives it is too late to contest that year's assessment, so a seller with a recent price drop should act before the deadline.

Unpaid parcels appear on a delinquent list published in a newspaper, then go to the annual tax sale. Buyers register by the date on the key dates list, file a letter of intent and pay a $250 registration fee that is applied to purchases. New buyers also need a letter of credit from their bank.

A sale does not move the deed. It places the unpaid tax in a buyer's hands, and the owner can pay it back during a redemption period. Ask the treasurer or clerk for the redemption deadline and payoff figure on any sold parcel before you list or sign a contract.

Mobile homes follow a separate track. Bills are mailed between March and May for the calendar year and are due 60 days after mailing. Interest runs $25 per month, capped at $100. A buyer needs a Mobile Home Certification filed with the Secretary of State to get clear title, and the treasurer can issue it once taxes are paid.

Start with the parcel's tax history and ask your title company how both installments will be handled at closing. Then look at deadlines and paperwork.

  • Pull the parcel record on the county portal and confirm the bill name and mailing address.
  • Ask the treasurer whether any installment shows penalty and what the payoff is on a given day.
  • Check whether an appeal is open, since the 2026 filing window runs to December 14.
  • Gather repair estimates and any appraisal, since both support an appeal and a price discussion.

A home needing repairs can go to a cash buyer as is, and a tax payoff is taken from the sale proceeds.

What to bring when you visit the courthouse: your parcel number, the original bill if you still have it, and a photo ID. The treasurer in Room 124 can give you the payoff on a given day, and the Supervisor of Assessments can tell you which exemptions sit on the parcel. Do both before the title company orders its payoff, so the figures match. If the buyer is financing, the lender will usually want proof that both installments for the year are paid or escrowed.

faqs.q: When is the Coles County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: The first installment is due around July 1 and the second around September 1. A 1.5% penalty applies to payments postmarked after the due date.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Coles County assessment complaint?
faqs.a: With the Supervisor of Assessments office in the courthouse at 651 Jackson Ave, Charleston, during weekday office hours. The Board of Review meets in Room 133. The 2026 filing deadline is December 14, 2026.

faqs.q: Can I pay Coles County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Yes. The treasurer accepts most credit and debit cards in the office, by phone and online. The card company charges a convenience fee, and an online check costs $1.00.

faqs.q: What is the Coles County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is the yearly auction of unpaid real estate tax, held in late October at 11:30 a.m. Buyers pay a $250 registration fee, and owners keep a redemption period to pay the amount back.

faqs.q: Does an appeal lower my Coles County tax bill right away?
faqs.a: No. An appeal challenges the assessed value, and any change flows into a later bill. You must keep paying while a state Property Tax Appeal Board case is pending.
